messages.author: 2e08631440d5f269
messages.subject: Interactive Point Click
parts:
I've been fiddling with the interactive framework by way of clicking on a graph to select information on a specific item (group). My current setup has the y-axis ranging from 0 to 1 (reflecting probability of answering the item correctly), and the x-axis ranging from -5 to 5 (representing ability). When I look at the coordinate information from the clicked object, the x-axis only ranges between 0 and 1 even when I click around +5. As a result, my click information is not very accurate. I'm wondering if this is a bug, a limitation of the interactive shiny options, or an error on my part?

I made a MWE in this gist: https://gist.github.com/lebebr01/5711d0123cd1341ba05f

Thank you in advance for any help.
Brandon

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Interactive Point Click
parts:
Hi Brandon -

I think the issue is that at the end of the code in renderPlot(), you call print(f). The renderPlot() code actually needs to return the plot object for interactive graphics to work properly, so you should just end the code with f, instead of print(f).

We'll try to make that clearer in the documentation.

-Winston
